bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Startup engagements are monetised via cash+equity or pure equity (cost-plus equity model), effectively building an investee portfolio, while corporates are monetised in cash — the CEO frames shareholder exposure as 'more analogous to a leveraged mutual fund than a standard mutual fund.'
- Portfolio of 12 investee companies carried at a cumulative cost of Rs 79,803.72 thousand, with combined fair value of Rs 726.76 million as of June 30, 2026, up from Rs 531.85 million a year earlier.
- Active reinvestment into venture-studio holdings: Biome raising INR 8 Cr for Zoop.Money at ~INR 80 Cr valuation (4.4x uplift) and increasing its OsteoForge commitment to INR 4 Cr (versus an initially planned INR 2 Cr) for a 10% combined stake, after OsteoForge's valuation rose 2.5x to INR 100 Cr within five months.
- Shareholding as on June 30, 2026: Promoters 50.61%, Others 49.39%.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Operates a dual model: acts like a tech co-founder for startups under a cost-plus equity arrangement (earning equity akin to stock options), and as a cash-paid enabler/consultant for corporates doing end-to-end innovation projects rather than 'body shopping.'
- Investment Rationale slide: a differentiated technology-services play focused on Data Science, AI and ML, with the ability to identify unique business models and partner with entrepreneurs to bring ideas to fruition.
- XELP Network Ecosystem / 'Multidimensional Innovation Matrix': 1000+ corporate and startup connects plus an experienced, multi-faceted team, enabling faster innovation cycles and cross-application of solutions across the startup network.
- Stated vision is to partner and grow with start-ups while selectively working on traditional projects, prioritising shareholder value creation over a consistent traditional growth story.
- Global reach beyond India highlighted via 'Existing Ventures/Projects' and 'Prospective Engagements' sections, consistent with the Q1FY27 revenue geographic split skewed to International.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [RELY Commercial Launch] Flagship Agetech platform for the Assisted/Senior Living ecosystem went live in Q1FY27 with three customers onboarded, marking an important commercialisation milestone.

- [Portfolio traction] Pencil signed a $950K, 36-month service deal with Alphabet/Google and has four AI-enabled products (audio, assessment, pitch bible, screenplay, proof-reading) due within 180 days (by Oct'26); The Star In Me (TSIM) won a Gold 'Startup of the Year' award at the ET Human Capital Annual Awards 2025.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.
